summary: B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, and delegates to FilesService.Add. A introduces explicitly prohibited association fields and bypasses Add while changing unrelated retry and reader-ownership semantics.
reasons: B encodes field "file" with the supplied filename through the established multipartbody.NewFile helper.
B returns s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving existing option handling, request construction, decoding, and error behavior as required.
A calls a new NewFileWithFields helper and duplicates Add's request/response implementation instead of routing Upload through Add.

A adds WithFilesFormFields and association-field support despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain unchanged everywhere else, including options ignored by other methods versus consumed by Upload behavior change concerns? Clarify: behavior changed by new option machinery can affect API surface. More direct explicit violation indeed. Also raw retry changes broad semantics and Add os.File behavior. B unrelated Persons. Need compact. Source reader NewFile propagates. Validation test absent in B, error reader absent. A validation but also error reader absent. B test uses io.NopCloser which is non-seekable and confirms calls but doesn't inspect multipart bytes second attempt. A does inspect second only, uses strings Reader content buffered. Contract says streamed content perhaps nonseekable—A upload retry uses strings.Reader but NewFile consumes it anyway so replay body bytes.
risks_a: Broad changes to RawClient body replay alter behavior for every seekable request body, including closure ownership and Content-Length, contrary to the contract's scope limits.
The seek-based GetBody closure reuses one mutable reader across attempts, adding concurrency and transport-lifecycle risk.
A still lacks an explicit source-reader failure test.
risks_b: It unnecessarily adds PersonsService.UploadPicture and tests, which are outside the requested scope.
Upload tests omit validation and source-reader error cases required by the contract.
The multipart test verifies filename but never reads and checks the uploaded content; the retry test counts attempts but does not verify the multipart body is intact after retry.
